newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Frepaso responds to "subversion" slur.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Frepaso responds to "subversion" slur.

text.p: Argentina's center-left coalition Frepaso hit back at the Peronist government Thursday for accusing it of association with violent groups of leftists who took part in riots this week.

Sen. Graciela Fernandez Meijide, one of the leaders of the Frepaso which has become the ruling Peronists' chief rival in national and city elections, told reporters: "They are ideological terrorists."

Senior Peronist officials launched a ferocious attack on the Frepaso for its support of a strike by teachers' union CTERA in the southern province of Neuquen, which turned violent this weekend with a woman bystander shot dead.

Frepaso leaders took part in a march in Buenos Aires Monday to protest at the death, blamed on police. The march was peaceful but a small group of activists of the radical leftist group Quebracho broke off and smashed the windows of the Neuquen government's offices in the capital.
The Peronists' chief whip in the lower house of Congress, Jorge Matzkin, commented Wednesday: "It would seem Quebracho has Frepaso as a political wing and CTERA as its union wing."
Social Development Secretary Eduardo Amadeo angered Frepaso leaders even more by saying: "Frepaso has the death it was looking for."

Menem talked of "old subversives...defended by political sectors" and rather bizarrely of "presubversive gymnastics." He even evoked the tactics of the brutal 1976-83 military rule by warning Argentine parents: "Look after your children."
Rodolfo Terragno, head of the opposition Radical Party, said Menem's words reminded him of "the tragic rhetoric of the military juntas."
Opposition politicians believe Menem is trying to raise the specter of "subversion" to strengthen his party ahead of October's mid-term elections in Congress.
"As we're in an election year, what's happening to Menem and all the Peronists is that their absolute majority in Congress is at risk," said Fernandez Meijide.
